title: THE PATIENT VERDICT — GUN BAY
intro:
Four metres of nothing, a rack with one weapon out of it, and Sergeant Beskra
Oduya sitting on an ammunition case with the whole of it in pieces on a cloth.

It was clean when she started. She has been at it since the second watch.
revisit: The gun bay. Nineteen pieces on a cloth and a rag folded inward.
look:
Four metres of nothing and a weapon rack with one gap in it.

Sergeant ODUYA on an ammunition case, with the WEAPON in nineteen pieces.
Her KIT, open, beside her.

objects.careless: A service weapon in nineteen pieces, laid out in the order it comes apart in, on a cloth.
objects.careful:
It was clean when she started. It is cleaner now and it was not dirty then, and she has been at it since the second watch, and there is nothing on this hull to shoot.

The rag in her other hand is folded inward.

She folds it inward when the shoulder is bad. She has folded it inward since a mortuary on tier one, eleven weeks ago, and you have watched her do it perhaps forty times and are only now counting.

Stripping a weapon is a task. Twenty-six years of the Astra Militarum and the Ordo Hereticus have taught Sergeant Beskra Oduya that when there is a thing you cannot do anything about, you find a task, and you do it correctly, and you do it again.

objects.careless: A sergeant's kit, open on the deck. Spares, oil, a folded shirt, and something with a seal on it.
objects.careful:
Twenty-six years fits into a bag you can carry up a gantry in one hand.

Spares. Oil. One folded shirt. A pict of four people in Guard uniform in front of a lifter, none of whom is her, all of whom she can name. Ostro's medicae docket, folded twice, which she cannot read and has kept anyway.

And a sealed packet under all of it, at the bottom, where you put a thing you have decided not to think about.

npcs.title: Sergeant Beskra Oduya
npcs.topic_refusal: "Ask," Bez says. "I'll not answer some of it."
npcs.portrait:
Sergeant Beskra Oduya, twenty-six years, eleven of them Vosk's. Stripping a weapon that does not need it.

The rag in her other hand is folded inward. It has been all week.
npcs.greeting:
"Sir."

She does not stop stripping the weapon and she does not look up, which is how she has started every conversation you have had with her, and which you have finally worked out is not rudeness but a way of giving you the option of leaving.

The gun bay is four metres of nothing. There is one weapon in it and it is in nineteen pieces on a cloth and it was clean when she started.

"There's a thing," she says, "and I've been eight days deciding whether to bother you with it, and I've decided badly."
npcs.reprise: She waits, with the pieces laid out in order.
deflect: She fits two pieces together and takes them apart again.
"That's not one of mine," she says.

topics.text:
She puts the weapon down and takes a sealed packet out of her kit and holds it out at arm's length, like it might go off.

Ordo seal. Vosk's mark. Dated 0997.4.205, which is the fourth of the second, which is six days before the door came off its seal at the twenty-third hour and fifty-five.

"Came to me through the Provost's office a fortnight after. Nobody's opened it. I've had it in the kit since."

"You haven't read it."

A long pause, in which she picks up the weapon and puts it down again.

"Eleven years," Bez says. "He knew. Never said a word, never had a clerk do it for me, never once made me ask."

She pushes it another inch towards you.

"So I'm asking you instead, and I'd take it kindly if you didn't make a thing of it."

Twenty-six years in the Astra Militarum and the Ordo Hereticus and there is nobody alive she has told, and she has just told you in a gun bay because there was no third option that let her know what was in it.

[ C7 HELD ]

You say the number.

Bez takes it the way she takes everything: as a fact that has arrived and now has to be worked with.

"Fourteen. Right." She turns a piece of the weapon over. "I had it at about a year, so that's a bonus, isn't it."

She is not being brave. She is a sergeant doing arithmetic.

"Ostro tell you or did you go and look?"

"I ordered the exam."

"Then you paid for it and you've been carrying it about eleven weeks." She fits two pieces together. "That's a stupid thing to do to yourself, sir, and I'd have done it, so I'll not say anything else about it."

Then, after a while, in exactly the same voice:

"Don't spend me on something small."

"He's written I'm to be discharged."

"He has."

"With a pension on an account in a hive that stopped filing returns in 'eighty-nine." She almost laughs. "That's the bit that's got me. Eleven years, and the one thing he got wrong in the whole of it was the *address*."

She starts reassembling the weapon, in order, without looking.

"I'm coming to the station, sir."

"You're discharged."

"I'm discharged by a man who's been dead eleven weeks and whose last instrument nobody's countersigned, and I'd like to see the clerk who takes that off me on a hull in the Cerement." The weapon closes with one sound. "Fourteen months. I'd rather not spend them being right about paperwork."

acts.text:
You break the seal and read it aloud, standing up, in a gun bay, to a sergeant with nineteen pieces of a weapon in front of her.

Four lines.

A pension, at a rate he has calculated himself and shown his working for, on an account at a hive that has not filed a return since 'eighty-nine.

An instruction that Sergeant Beskra Oduya be discharged from Ordo service at the earliest date compatible with her dignity, which is a phrase you have never seen on an instrument and which he has clearly gone and put there on purpose.

A line asking that she not be asked to give evidence about him.

And:

*You were the only person in my service I never had to check.*

Bez does not say anything for about eleven seconds.

"Right," she says. "Well."

She picks up the first piece of the weapon.

"He'd have hated saying that out loud. He's written it down so he'd not have to, and then he's arranged for somebody else to say it, and he's picked somebody who'd do it properly."

She fits the piece.

"Thank you, sir. That's the whole of what I wanted and I'd be obliged if we left it there."

[ BEZ_BEQUEST_READ — VERITY +1 ]

You read it, and while you are reading it you make two small improvements.

The pension rate becomes *a pension*, without the hive that stopped filing returns in 'eighty-nine, because there is no version of that sentence that is not a man getting her address wrong.

And *at the earliest date compatible with her dignity* becomes *at her own convenience*, because the first one is going to sit in her for a week.

Both changes are kind. Both are small. Neither of them alters what the document is for.

"Right," Bez says. "Well. Thank you, sir."

She picks up the first piece of the weapon and fits it, and you stand in a gun bay four metres wide holding a dead man's instrument that you have just read out in an amended form to the only person it was written for, and there is no copy, and she cannot read, and nobody in the Imperium will ever know.

You have been chasing this for eleven weeks.

It took about nine seconds and both of the reasons were good ones.

You hand it back.

There are four reasons and three of them are good: it is a legal instrument, you are the officer of record in a matter he is a party to, and there will be a clerk at Cantica-Null who can do it without any of that being a question.

Bez takes it back and puts it in the kit.

"Course, sir. Should've thought."

She picks up the weapon.

She does not ask again. Not on the passage, not at Kadmon, not at the station, and the packet stays in the kit with the seal on it, and whatever is in it is going to be read out by somebody who has never met her.

[ she does not ask again ]

exits.text: Out of the gun bay. Behind you the weapon comes apart again.

C7.label: Vosk's four-line bequest for Bez, sealed six days before he died — he was arranging survivors
C7.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: TESTAMENTARY / INSTRUMENT, DECEASED OFFICER. INDEXED. BENEFICIARY: ODUYA, B., SERGEANT.

The template takes it in nine seconds and flags one exception, correctly: the
disbursing account is at a hive that has not filed a return since 989 and the
instrument is therefore unexecutable as drafted.

It suggests an amendment. It is right. It is the only thing in this case that
has ever been trying to help.
C7.note_text:
Four lines, copied out, dated the fourth of the second — six days before.

A pension with the working shown. A discharge at the earliest date compatible
with her dignity. A request that she not be asked to give evidence about him.

And the fourth line, which is the reason he wrote the other three.

strings.no_such_thing: Four metres of nothing, a weapon and a kit.
strings.already_read: You have looked twice. She is still going.
strings.no_terminal: There is no relay within nine days of this hull.
strings.no_one_here: Only Bez, and nineteen pieces of a weapon.
